crafts.name: Plastic Bird Feeder
instructions: Wash the bottle and dry it completely
Cut small holes on the lower part of the bottle
Insert the wooden spoons through the holes
Cut out bigger holes above the spoons
Fill the bottle with birdseed or rice
Hang the bird feeder outside
crafts.sustainability_note: Plastic is lightweight and waterproof, making it suitable for outdoor use.

crafts.name: Stationery Holder
instructions: Remove stickers from the plastic bottle
Cut off the bottle's neck, leaving the bottom section
Paint the lower part of the bottle and add decorative items if desired
Add stationery and your holder is complete!
crafts.sustainability_note: The plastic is waterproof, protecting stationery, and lightweight, making the holder easy to move.
environmental_benefits: Reduces the need to buy a stationery holder from a store

crafts.name: Mini Basket
instructions: Cut the bottom half of the bottle, which will become the body of the basket
Paint and decorate it with desired colours and designs
Take the other half of the bottle and cut out a thick strip of plastic
Paint and decorate the strip
Hot glue the ends of the strip to the sides of the basket to create a handle
Add final touches and your basket is complete!
crafts.sustainability_note: The lightweight plastic is portable and durable, making it suitable for a reusable decorative basket.
environmental_benefits: Prevents harmful chemicals from entering the environment

crafts.name: DIY Hanging Wall Decor
instructions: Collect dry plastic bottles and remove the stickers
Cut the bottles into plastic sheets
Cut out desired shapes such as flowers, leaves, or stars
Paint the shapes
Hot glue them onto the cord
Hang the decoration on your wall!
crafts.sustainability_note: Multiple plastic bottles are recycled and transformed into a decorative wall hanging.
environmental_benefits: Prevents harmful toxins and chemicals from leaking into the environment

crafts.name: Plastic Bottle Plant Pot
instructions: Make sure the plastic bottle is clean and dry
Use a marker to draw a line around the bottle about halfway up
Carefully cut along the line to separate the top and bottom of the bottle
Keep the bottom half of the bottle, which will become the plant pot
Carefully poke small holes in the bottom of the bottle to allow extra water to drain
Decorate the outside of the bottle with paint, markers, or other recycled materials
Fill the bottle with soil
Plant a small seed or place a small plant into the soil
Add a little water and place the plant pot somewhere with enough sunlight
Watch your plant grow in its new recycled home!
crafts.sustainability_note: Plants need sunlight, water, air, and nutrients from soil to grow. Drainage holes help prevent excess water from damaging plant roots while giving the plastic bottle a new purpose.
environmental_benefits: Reuses a plastic bottle that might otherwise become waste
Gives an everyday item a useful second life
Encourages kids to grow plants and care for nature
Teaches the importance of recycling and responsible consumption
